+import os
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+from click.testing import CliRunner
+
+from dotenv.cli import cli
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="requires Unix symlinks")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("command", ["set", "unset"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "flag,follow",
+    [([], False), (["--follow-symlinks"], True), (["--no-follow-symlinks"], False)],
+)
+def test_mutation_symlink_policy(tmp_path, command, flag, follow):
+    target = tmp_path / "target.env"
+    target.write_text("a=old\nb=keep\n")
+    link = tmp_path / ".env"
+    link.symlink_to(target)
+    tail = ["a", "new"] if command == "set" else ["a"]
+    result = CliRunner().invoke(
+        cli, ["--file", str(link), command, *flag, *tail]
+    )
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+    expected = "a='new'\nb=keep\n" if command == "set" else "b=keep\n"
+    assert link.is_symlink() is follow
+    if follow:
+        assert target.read_text() == expected
+    else:
+        assert target.read_text() == "a=old\nb=keep\n"
+        assert link.read_text() == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="requires Unix symlinks")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("flag,follow", [([], False), (["--follow-symlinks"], True)])
+def test_set_dangling_symlink_policy(tmp_path, flag, follow):
+    target = tmp_path / "missing.env"
+    link = tmp_path / ".env"
+    link.symlink_to(target)
+    result = CliRunner().invoke(
+        cli, ["--file", str(link), "set", *flag, "a", "new"]
+    )
+    assert result.exit_code == 0, result.output
+    assert link.is_symlink() is follow
+    assert target.exists() is follow
+    assert (target if follow else link).read_text() == "a='new'\n"

spec.question: Expose the library's symlink policy on the CLI mutation commands. Add command-specific `--follow-symlinks/--no-follow-symlinks` options to `dotenv set` and `dotenv unset`, defaulting to not following symlinks. Pass the selected policy to the existing library APIs without changing quote/export behavior, output, or exit statuses. Following an existing link must edit its target while preserving the link; the default must retain the current link-replacement behavior. For `set` on a dangling link, following must create the target and preserve the link, while not following must replace the link with the new dotenv file. Update the command help so it no longer implies that following links is impossible. Deliver a unified diff against production files only.
